Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. ## What this changes Prefer callable OpenClaw Ask User over Codex’s blocking question tool while preserving explicit native opt-ins and restricted-tool policy. **Example:** A Default-mode conversation with callable ask_user asks the user to choose Reporting or Billing. - **Before:** Codex can select request_user_input and reject the call as unavailable in Default mode. - **After:** The native blocking tool is disabled by default, leaving OpenClaw Ask User available for the question. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | The patch is focused and source-supported, with useful regression coverage; current evidence remains harness-based and exact-head CI is unfinished. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | This maintainer-authored PR is outside the ordinary contributor proof gate; current evidence exercises configuration and lifecycle harnesses, while older live-proof reports do not establish this head’s behavior. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Product **Kind:** Bug fix · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** A Codex conversation can choose a blocking question tool that rejects the question before the user sees it. **Reason:** The failure is source-backed, the existing OpenClaw tool supplies the needed capability, and maintainer authorship establishes direction. ## Merge readiness ✅ **Ready for maintainer review** Keep open: this maintainer-authored PR addresses a current Codex question-tool failure, and source review found no actionable introduced defect. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `48701f966b6f79e92791319914d4606856742b51` ## Before merge None. ## Findings None. ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: No current-head shipped-entry-point replay or latest-stable upgrade run is supplied; the body records base-red/head-green proof for the callable-default and supervised-question regressions.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The Codex plugin translates OpenClaw tool availability and native configuration into app-server start, resume, and fork requests; accepted questions then use the existing interactive delivery paths. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[OpenClaw turn tools] --> C[Thread configuration owner] B[Native configuration snapshot] --> C C --> D[Codex app server] D --> E[OpenClaw Ask User] E --> F[User answer] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep question selection in the existing thread-configuration owner, using actual executor availability and preserving authored native preferences. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source establishes the failure: the native blocking tool defaults on, Default-mode support defaults off, and the handler rejects before OpenClaw receives the question; no runtime execution was performed during this review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? This is a focused repair: it selects the usable existing tool through one configuration owner, reuses the preflight snapshot and refresh fingerprint, and leaves native opt-ins and restricted policy intact. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [16779ec57df8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/16779ec57df82bf752a5cd5b24f96659e442379e). ### Provenance checked - `Native questions and configuration preferences` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109724: Expose accepted native questions through existing structured presentation and request-scoped answer delivery.) - `Native configuration preservation` keeps the original intent (3f0b58e2696bfe229f96b1403bfd25f65992c584: Preserve local native configuration and established policy across supervised continuation.) - `Shared effective configuration snapshot` keeps the original intent (82d2c992a25bc38336e1a5d49e1ef15d03798f19: Use canonical native configuration facts for tool-policy and scheduled-capability handling.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security None. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Pinned introduced change:** Reviewed the merge-base-to-head hunks and original configuration code; the patch forwards executor availability into the existing configuration owner without adding persisted state. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-start.ts:113`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/48701f966b6f79e92791319914d4606856742b51/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-start.ts#L113), [48701f966b6f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/48701f966b6f79e92791319914d4606856742b51)) - **Preserved native preferences:** Authored values are resolved from the effective projection or the enabled raw layer matching the winning origin and version, addressing the earlier native-opt-in finding. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/config-layer-policy.ts:55`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/48701f966b6f79e92791319914d4606856742b51/extensions/codex/src/app-server/config-layer-policy.ts#L55), [48701f966b6f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/48701f966b6f79e92791319914d4606856742b51)) - **Personally inspected dependency contract:** The patch consumes Codex’s configuration protocol and depends on its tool-registration contract. The inspected sibling source defaults the blocking tool to enabled, gates Default-mode support separately, rejects unavailable modes before emitting a user-input request, and registers async questions independently. GitHub verified the sibling SHA belongs to openai/codex. ([`codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input.rs:74`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input.rs#L74), [092d3acd6bec](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d)) - **Current main still needs the selection policy:** Fetched main disables native blocking questions for restricted surfaces but lacks this PR’s callable Ask User selection for ordinary conversations. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-requests.ts:113`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/16779ec57df82bf752a5cd5b24f96659e442379e/extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-requests.ts#L113), [16779ec57df8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/16779ec57df82bf752a5cd5b24f96659e442379e)) - **Existing conversation refresh:** The existing fingerprint includes resulting request configuration, and warm reuse falls back to resume when that fingerprint changes; the added lifecycle coverage exercises authored-setting and executor-availability transitions. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-warm.ts:516`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/48701f966b6f79e92791319914d4606856742b51/extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-warm.ts#L516), [48701f966b6f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/48701f966b6f79e92791319914d4606856742b51)) - **Related report and historical intent:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/119333 documents the same Default-mode rejection. Prior native-question work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109724 and native-configuration preservation in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151001 support retaining accepted native questions and authored preferences. Likely related people: - **Peter Steinberger:** Raw commit 82d2c992a25bc38336e1a5d49e1ef15d03798f19 adds extensions/codex/src/app-server/config-layer-policy.ts:25 relative to its recorded parents. Label justifications: - `P2`: A bounded question-tool contract failure can prevent structured questions, while ordinary conversational recovery remains possible. - `rating: 🦐 gold shrimp`: Overall readiness is 🦐 gold shrimp; proof is 🦐 gold shrimp and patch quality is 🐚 platinum hermit. - `status: 👀 ready for maintainer look`: ClawSweeper has no concrete contributor-facing blocker left for this PR. ### Rank-up moves Optional improvements that raise the rating; they are not merge blockers. - For stronger confidence, replay a Default-mode question in an existing conversation after upgrading from stable, checking both default selection and an authored native opt-in. ### Rating scale 6/6 🦀 challenger crab · 5/6 🦞 diamond lobster · 4/6 🐚 platinum hermit · 3/6 🦐 gold shrimp · 2/6 🦪 silver shellfish · 1/6 🧂 unranked krab.
